steps.text:
On day one, we recommend starting with ball mastery.

• **It's one of the most important skills you can learn.**

• **You don't need any equipment.**

• **You can do it in your living room, your garage, or out on the field.**

Here are a few ball mastery programs to get you started.
steps.label: Start with Ball Mastery

player.q: Do you recommend a training plan?

steps.label: Yes — But It Depends on Your Preference
steps.text:
Training plans are recurring and give you a guided path.

• **However, some users prefer sticking with a few folders and working through them at their own pace.**

• **I use both.**

• **I built a custom plan for my son's after-school training, and I favorite folders we use for longer training sessions.**

player.q: How long should my child train?

steps.label: The Key to Success: Train at a Level They Can Stick With
steps.text:
We call this **MEEE** — the Minimum Extra Effort they can do with Enthusiasm.

A few things to keep in mind:

• Consistency beats intensity — even **20 minutes a week** can meaningfully improve a player's skill

• **Sit down with your child and set a weekly goal together, one they can realistically handle**

• **Let them help pick the goal — a goal they chose is a goal they'll keep**

steps.label: No — With a Few Exceptions
steps.text:
The program stacks skills — one new move per video, each building on the last.

• **INTRO** — teaches a new move

• **QR** — quick review of recent moves

• **FR** — full review of a block

Reviews bring back earlier moves automatically, so your child can train on their own without you having to manage or re-teach anything. Skip a video, though, and later reviews may reference a move they missed.

**Exceptions:**

• **Strong jugglers can skip the early juggling build-up**

• **No space/equipment? Skip and return later**

player.q: Where do beginners and experienced players start?

steps.label: Everyone Starts in the Same Place
steps.text:
We recommend all players start with the first folders and follow the program in order.

• The difference between experienced players and beginners is in the levels of **volume, variety, and variations**.

steps.label: Beginner
steps.text: A beginner may start with only the 1,000 Touch Ball Mastery program.

steps.label: Experienced
steps.text: An experienced player can handle multiple ball mastery programs, as well as training programs in other skill areas.
This is just one example. A beginner may focus on one type of ball mastery, where an experienced player should do several types — while still following them in order.

steps.label: Same Start, More Volume and Variety
steps.text:
As mentioned before, experienced players should still start with the first folders — what changes is how much they take on and how quickly they add to it.

• Another way to accelerate that variety is our **30-Day Plans**

• **Each video works four to six different moves**

• **A player covers far more ground in the same session**

Start with:

steps.label: Test your juggling
steps.text:
The Skill Challenge gives you a number to train against — and something to beat next month. We are starting with juggling.

**⚽ How it works**

• **Set your ultimate goal — the number you are chasing.**

• **Every time you try, add a record: the ball you used, how many juggles, and the date.**

• **Your highest sits next to your goal, and the table keeps every attempt so you can watch it climb.**

**🎾 Three balls, three goals**

A regular ball, a size 1 ball and a tennis ball each keep their own goal and their own records — 100 with a tennis ball is a very different feat from 100 with a size 5.

player.q: Can I build my own plan?

steps.label: Yes! Three easy ways to do it
steps.text:
You do not have to use our plans as they come — you can pick your own videos and build a plan around exactly what your player needs.

• **Pin as you browse** — in **All Programs**, pin either a whole folder or a single video straight to your plan. Quickest route if you already know the programs you want.

• **Hand-pick the moves** — in **Search Key Skill Moves**, search for the skill you want to work on, pin the videos you like to **My Favorites**, then make a folder and add them to it. Best when you are choosing by what your player needs rather than by program.

• **Build a custom plan from folders** — pick the folders you want them working through and the plan is built from them. A middle ground: more structured than a pile of favourites, less work than picking every video by hand.

steps.label: Splitting it across the week
steps.text:
Worth knowing before you start: none of these split the work into days for you. The videos sit in the plan and your player works through them at their own pace.

If you want a day-by-day structure — say five days, each with its own focus — **make a folder per day**. Name them **Day 1**, **Day 2** and so on, put the right videos in each, and your player opens the folder for that day.

A little more setup at the start, and it gives you exact control over what they do on each day.

steps.label: How your player sees it
steps.text:
Once it is in their plan, they open it from **Training Plans** — there is nothing to send them.

If you get stuck at any step, use the **Help Line** and we will walk you through it.

steps.label: Finishing is where shooting lives
steps.text:
These drills live in two places: the **All Programs** section and the **Training Plans** section.

**🥅 What you need**

• **Bring several balls.** The follow-along videos leave time to collect your balls.

• **Something to shoot at.** A full size goal is ideal, but smaller goals or simple targets work just as well.

• **Change the set-up to suit you.** Move the cones closer or further out, shorten the run, adjust the distance from goal — whatever fits the space you have.

**💡 Bonus tip**

• Let the video run in the background and work at your own pace.

• The cadence and music keep it moving — the rest is your creativity.

• Add a defender, a keeper or a passing pattern to bring it closer to a game.

**📅 Make it a plan**

Below are some of our favourites. Find them all in the **All Programs** area, or build a **custom** or **30-day** finishing plan.

steps.q: Step 1: Start with 1,000 Touch Ball Mastery

steps.label: Get used to how the program works
steps.text:
1,000 Touch Ball Mastery is the best way to get used to the program and understand how it works — how the videos build on each other, how reviews bring earlier moves back, and how much a short session actually covers.

• **You don't need equipment or space.**

• **The moves stack, so you are learning the system as well as the skill.**

• **Once this feels familiar, everything else in the program makes sense.**

steps.q: Step 2: Decide how you will use the program

steps.label: Two things to decide
steps.text:
How you use the program comes down to two things:

• **Where you plan to train**

• **What skills you want to practice**

The next two steps cover each one.

steps.q: Step 3: Where you plan to train

steps.text:
You can use the program inside the home, outside, or both — plenty of players do both.

**At home or inside** — a garage, a hallway, a bedroom. Ten minutes before school, a few more after dinner. The goal is volume of touches, not a full session, and training inside works better than people expect.

**Outside / on the field** — with space and a goal you can train everything: finishing, passing over distance, full-speed dribbling and 1v1s. Use a training plan so the session has a shape rather than picking videos as you go.

steps.label: Recommendation for Using In-home
steps.text:
Pick from:

• **Ball Mastery**

• **Wall Passing**

• **Tight Space Dribbling**

• **Juggling** *

• **1v1 Moves** *

* These need modifying for indoor space — smaller touches, a softer or smaller ball, and no full-power strikes.

steps.q: Step 4: What skills you plan to practice

steps.text:
How many areas you take on should match the time you actually have.

• **One area** — 1,000 Touch Ball Mastery on its own is plenty to start, and builds the habit.

• **Two or three** — add wall passing or dribbling once ball mastery feels routine.

• **More than that** — only if you are training most days, or on the field with real time to fill.

Whichever you pick, work through each area in order rather than jumping around. The videos build on each other, and the reviews bring earlier moves back for you.
